actions.relational_constraint: Pin is located into the bearing area; pin axis should be aligned/coaxial with the bearing axis so the part can rotate around the pin. Pin should pass through both clevis ears without intersecting the slot inner walls; maintain intended running clearance between pin OD and bore ID for rotation.
actions.unresolved_reference: Pin functional spec not fully defined: confirm desired fit class (running clearance vs press), whether pin should protrude for fasteners, and whether the pin should be a separate assembly component. steps: Localize the bearing/bore: in Section S1 (Clevis / forked mounting end), select the pin-bore cylindrical bearing surface on one ear (face_code 0004 / Brep FACE 0) and/or the mirrored ear segment (face_code 0005 / Brep FACE 1). Create/derive a construction axis from these cylindrical faces (their cylinder axis is along global Y and defines the rotation axis).

Create a sketch plane normal to the pin axis: define a datum plane perpendicular to global Y that passes through the derived bore axis (equivalently, create a plane at the bore’s axial mid-plane). This plane is used to sketch the pin cross-section concentrically to the bore.

Sketch the pin profile: on the datum plane, sketch a circle centered on the bore axis. Dimension the circle to the intended pin diameter. Default is Ø6.00 mm to match the modeled bore radius (R3); if rotational clearance is intended, reduce to Ø5.95..Ø5.98 mm per fit requirement.

Create the pin solid as a new body: perform a symmetric extrusion of the circle along the pin axis (±Y) to the required overall length. At minimum, set extrusion depth to span the full outside clevis width (approx 16.38 mm from y=-8.19 to y=+8.19). If the design intent includes external retention (clips, washers, cotter), extend beyond the ear outer faces by the specified protrusion per side.

Check interference/clearance: verify the pin passes through both ear bore segments and that it does not collide with the clevis slot inner walls (face_code 0002 at y=-3.5 and face_code 0003 at y=+3.5) other than traversing the open slot region; confirm the pin is coaxial with faces 0004/0005.
Add end lead-ins: apply a small chamfer (e.g., 0.5 mm x 45°) or fillet (e.g., R0.5) to both pin end edges to ease assembly through the ear bores and reduce edge burr sensitivity.

Assembly/motion intent (if supported by the CAD system): define a revolute mate/joint where the pin is fixed (or grounded) and the link arm rotates about the pin axis, using the same cylindrical axis extracted from face_code 0004/0005 as the joint axis.
